newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks snap 11-day losing streak.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks snap 11-day losing streak.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed higher for the first time in two weeks as demand for brewer Bavaria S.A., blue-chip Banco Ganadero and undervalued cement shares helped the country's two leading indices eke out modest gains.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index closed up 0.12 percent at 14,780.36 on an active trading volume of 3.2 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB rose 0.48 percent, meanwhile, ending at 959.70 on moderate volume of 1.3 billion pesos.
"The markets have seen several days of (price) stabilization and it looks as though a rise is in the works," one Bogota-based broker said.
"The demand for Bavaria and cement companies indicates once again that clients are leaning toward solid ... shares" with good liquidity, he added.

Bavaria closed up 0.90 percent in Bogota and Medellin, at 5,600 pesos per share. A total more than 1.8 billion shares in the company changed hands amid what some brokers said were rumors of an upcoming share split. Others said the buying spree may simply have been fueled by talk of strong fourth-quarter earnings.
Shares of cement companies belonging to the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate were also in demand.

Cementos Argos closed up 1.15 percent in Medellin at 6,271.50 pesos per share and up 2.03 percent in Bogota at 6,250. Cementos Caribe rose 1.02 percent in Bogota to end at 4,950 and posted an almost identical gain in Medellin.

Brokers said both companies appeared undervalued at current levels, were attractive to foreign funds, and are expected to pay solid dividends this year. "The bad thing is that you sometimes can't find large quantities of their shares," one broker said.
The day's biggest winner was Ganadero, which saw its preferential shares jump 4.54 percent in Bogota to close at 230 pesos per share.
